<a id="body"></a>

## Body

Open when a current-daemon lease brake is proposed as all-interleaving protection.

F268 R2's original real-SQLite witnesses passed: no restart after a failed audit
when the current lease is already live; a later real expiry has its own edge and
restart. Three mutants independently restored those failures or lost audit retry.

The scope has two boundaries. Fresh delivery service on the same durable state
has no lease-map proof until reattachment/heartbeat: stale lapse plus boot grace
queued one restart; current heartbeat before reconcile spared it even when its
audit failed. Initial native attestation/registration also creates the map entry,
so "renewed" is not necessarily an observed heartbeat.

A deterministic liveness latch proved a second ordering: brake returned false,
then the receiver renewed with a failed audit while decision work awaited
liveness. Releasing it still queued one restart. A snapshot brake does not span
later awaits. Do not repair it by blindly holding the global native mutex across
control admission; inspect the lock order.

Both are new C34 follow-ups, not R2 regressions; original witnesses remain green.
Magic wand: keep boot and renewal-during-decision controls beside producer retry
tests, so future claims name exactly when their evidence applies.
